mujahada.lead: Spiritual striving (mujāhada) and steadfastness (istiqāma) are the two wings with which the seeker flies towards Allah’s pleasure and nearness; without them he cannot rise. The more you strive, the more paths Allah opens for you that lead to His pleasure.

secs.t: What are striving and steadfastness?
secs.h:
Striving means giving all the effort you are capable of, and steadfastness means carrying on along the way. If you fall, you get up again — for the real fall is not falling down, but failing to stand up again.

In other words:

  • Striving: mastering the soul that commands evil, and its desires, through strength of will.
  • Steadfastness: persevering in good deeds and keeping away from wrongdoing, whatever your inner feelings or outer circumstances.

secs.t: The evidence from the Quran and the Sunnah
secs.h:
“Indeed, those who say ‘Our Lord is Allah’ and then remain steadfast — the angels descend upon them: ‘Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive the good news of Paradise, which you were promised.’” (Fuṣṣilat 41:30)

Abū ʿAmr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “O Messenger of Allah, tell me something about Islam that I will not need to ask anyone else about.” He replied: “Say: I believe in Allah — then be steadfast.” (Muslim)

secs.t: Why does the seeker need striving?
secs.h:
The moment a person starts drawing near to Allah, he declares war on:

  • his own ego;
  • Satan;
  • bad company;
  • love of this world and its distractions.

All of these become his enemies. They may even use his friends, his family and others to turn him away from the path of truth and the Prophetic Sunnah, through many tricks: criticism, mockery, belittling and pressure.

If he is not prepared to face and bear these difficulties, it is as though he has laid down his weapons and written failure for himself — unless he changes course.

secs.t: The three conditions of striving
secs.h:
Striving rests on three pillars; without them it is mere wishful thinking. Picture it as a bird: its two wings are will and effort, and its head is Allah’s help.

Willthe first wingAllah’s helpthe head that guidesEffortthe second wing
  1. Seeking the help of Allah Most High: acknowledge your own weakness, poverty and helplessness, then rely on Him.
  2. Resolve: firmly decide to hold yourself back from sins — not merely wish for it.
  3. Effort: do everything within your power to avoid falling into sin, and keep up good deeds.

secs.t: Wishing versus will
secs.h:
Wishing: “I wish Allah were pleased with me and that I became His close friend, but I am not ready to pay the price or to sacrifice anything.” That is wishful thinking.

Will: “I will do my utmost to reach my goal, and I will sacrifice my desires.” In other words: I will purify my body, mind, heart and lower self from sins, and adorn my body, mind and heart with the beautiful qualities and noble character of the Messenger ﷺ.

Wishingno price paidno climbing, no toilno sacrificeno journey on Allah’s pathResult: no fruit — and nearness to this world and to Satan
Willa price paidclimbing and toilsacrificea journey on Allah’s pathResult: the fruit is gathered — and nearness to Allah

Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The wise one is he who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death; and the helpless one is he who follows his whims and then indulges in wishful hopes from Allah.” (al-Tirmidhī, Book of the Description of the Resurrection, no. 2459, ḥasan)

tawba.lead: Repentance (tawba) means returning: turning back from a life full of sins to the path of righteousness, from evil to good. It is a door that leads the servant into the Garden of Refuge, and Allah loves those who repent and return to His path. It is the way to mend the relationship between the servant and his Creator — and whoever does not mend his relationship with Allah will gain nothing from any other relationship.

secs.t: The four conditions of repentance
secs.h:
1. Remorse: to be filled with regret and shame for the sin committed, small or great — every sin leaves a dark stain on the heart, even disliked acts.
  2. Cutting off the roads to sin: blocking every path that leads to it and keeping away from whatever drags you into darkness, such as bad company or the misuse of television and the internet.
  3. Sincere resolve: a pure intention and determination never to return to the darkness, and real effort to walk the straight path.
  4. Restoring rights: fulfilling the rights of Allah, of the Messenger ﷺ and of creation, and humbly asking forgiveness for any you violated. Nor should you neglect the rights of your own self, or you will remain in the darkness of sin.

secs.t: Fulfilling rights and redressing wrongs
secs.h:
It is a beautiful thing to want to spend the rest of your life in complete obedience to Allah, following the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ. But if in the past you violated the rights of Allah, of the Messenger ﷺ, of your own self or of other people, you must redress those wrongs and ask Allah’s forgiveness.

First: the rights of Allah

  1. Never associate anyone with Him, in His essence or in His attributes.
  2. Worship Him to gain His pleasure alone — not for fame or a good name among people.
  3. Make up every obligatory prayer you missed, and ask Allah’s forgiveness.
  4. Make up every obligatory fast you missed or left incomplete, and pay its expiation as the Sharia prescribes.
  5. Calculate the obligatory zakat you missed in past years and pay it.
  6. Perform the Hajj in the coming season if it is obligatory upon you.
  7. If you swore an oath or made a vow to Allah and did not keep it, you must fulfil it or pay the expiation, and repent.

Second: the rights of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

  1. Complete and wholehearted faith in Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
  2. Loving him ﷺ more than your spouse, your children, your parents and everything else.
  3. Honouring, revering and exalting him, and everything connected to him: his religion, his Sunnah and his life.
  4. Following his religion, his law and his Sunnah — living your life as he lived his ﷺ.
  5. Inviting others to the Sharia, the Sunnah and his life ﷺ, and conveying them to people.

Third: the rights of your own self

  1. Save yourself from Allah’s displeasure and from the punishment of Hell.
  2. Look after the health of your body.
  3. Give your body enough sleep and rest.
  4. Keep your body pure and clean.
  5. Feed yourself from what is lawful.

Fourth: the rights of people — of three kinds

  1. Financial rights: anything to do with money and property. If in the past you gained anything unlawfully — land, property, gold, silver or anything else — you must return it to its owners or ask them to forgive you. If the owner has died, return it to his heirs; if he has no heirs, give it in charity on his behalf.
  2. Rights over body and life: if you harmed anyone physically, emotionally or mentally, you must ask them to pardon you.
  3. Rights of honour and reputation: such as false accusation, backbiting, tale-bearing, false testimony, mocking or belittling your fellow Muslim. You must ask them to pardon and forgive you.

After asking people to pardon you, turn humbly to Allah for His forgiveness, and repent to Him, fulfilling the conditions of repentance.

You must also repent to Allah if you killed or harmed an animal, a bird or an insect without just cause.

Finally, call upon Allah with the Master Supplication for Forgiveness (Sayyid al-Istighfār):

“O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin — so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.” (al-Bukhārī)

secs.t: The rights at a glance
secs.h:
Rights owed toWhat they include
AllahPure monotheism, sincerity, zakat, Hajj, oaths, vows, love, servanthood, obedience and reverence
The Messenger of Allah ﷺFaith, love, honour, reverence, following his Sunnah and conveying his message
Your own selfProtecting it from punishment in the Hereafter, caring for its health, lawful earning and purity
PeopleMaterial and moral respect, and keeping promises
The rest of creation: the environment, the earth, living beings and natural resourcesMercy, causing no harm, and no waste or extravagance with blessings

secs.t: The two rakʿas of repentance
secs.h:
The penitent makes a proper ablution, then prays two rakʿas for the sake of Allah, weeping from the depths of his heart as he remembers his sins, filled with deep self-reproach and remorse, and he supplicates with the Master Supplication for Forgiveness: “O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You…”

He sends blessings and peace upon the Messenger ﷺ before and after the prayer.

The best time is the last third of the night, when Allah Most High says: “Is there anyone seeking forgiveness?”

secs.t: Never stop or postpone repentance
secs.h:
It is important to fulfil the conditions of repentance, and to remember that you must intend never to commit the sin again. Yet this is not a binding promise: if you sin again, you return to the conditions of repentance once more.

And if you cannot give the sin up, you must never abandon repentance, for Allah loves those who repent — and no one is free of sin except the Messenger ﷺ and the angels.

secs.t: Satan’s deception about repentance
secs.h:
To carry on sinning without repenting while hoping for forgiveness is pure self-deception, foolishness and wishful thinking. The right way is to take the means, then rely on Allah.

No one expects a harvest without first sowing the seeds: repentance is the sowing, and forgiveness is the fruit.

secs.t: Until when can a person repent?
secs.h:
A person can repent until the moment of the death agony arrives — before his soul leaves him and his breathing stops.

And the door of repentance remains open to all people until the sun rises from the west.

secs.t: Key points: when is repentance not valid?
secs.h:
Sincerity comes first: leave the sin for Allah’s sake alone — not out of fear of blame or of anything else. So these are not valid repentance:

  • Someone who leaves a sin for the sake of a job or a position.
  • Someone who leaves it for the sake of people.
  • Someone who leaves it to avoid illness or out of fear for his health.
  • Someone who stops stealing because he could not get into the house or the safe, or out of fear of guards or the police.
  • Someone who gives up drugs or alcohol because he is poor.
  • Someone kept from sin by an outside factor — such as impotence that keeps him from fornication, or blindness that keeps him from forbidden glances.

secs.t: What helps you stay firm in repentance
secs.h:
1. Leaving the sin outwardly and inwardly: outwardly by abandoning it, and inwardly by no longer thinking about it — not reliving its pleasure or the thrill of past sins, nor wishing to go back to them, or you will surely return to that road.
  2. Giving up the minor sins: for minor sins lead to major ones — lustful glances, for example, lead to fornication.
  3. Keeping away from every road that leads to sin, such as alcohol and anything obscene, and the scenes and distractions that pull you towards them.
  4. Leaving the environment that makes sin easy.
  5. Leaving bad company, and keeping the company of the pious, who help and support you in every good deed.
  6. Being wary of what makes leaving hard: some sins give a person great standing — a gang leader or a celebrity, for instance — which makes them hard to abandon.
  7. Not postponing repentance: death may come suddenly, and the heart may be sealed. Remember that postponing repentance is itself a sin that must be repented of.
  8. Fear and hope together: always fear that your repentance is lacking or incomplete; do not feel sure that you have been forgiven, but hope for Allah’s mercy and keep asking His forgiveness.
  9. Attending gatherings of remembrance and exhortation, and visiting graves to remember the Hereafter.
  10. Keeping the company of a righteous, devout guide who helps you cleanse yourself of sins and reach nearness to Allah and His pleasure, through correcting the self.
  11. Renewing the body’s strength through what is lawful: spend the energy and strength that came from unlawful earnings in Allah’s way, so that you begin building your energy and strength through lawful means.

secs.t: Doubts and whispers that keep people from repenting
secs.h:
Among the common whispers:

  • “I want to repent, but who can guarantee that Allah has forgiven me?”
  • “My sins are too many to be forgiven.”

The answer: you are not the one who forgives — Allah is. So never abandon repentance, for you will need it every time you fall into sin. You are not sinless like the angels, nor steeped in wrongdoing like Satan; you are a human being with a free and strong will that can rise above the angels and be stronger than any devil that tries to sway you. Hold to the path of mindfulness of Allah, for Allah forgives whoever repents sincerely, and His mercy outstrips His wrath.

Allah Most High says in a ḥadīth qudsī: “O son of Adam, even if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and then you asked My forgiveness, I would forgive you, and I would not mind.”

A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “What of a man who has committed every sin and left nothing undone — is there repentance for him?” He ﷺ said: “Have you embraced Islam?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then do good deeds and leave bad deeds, and Allah will turn them all into good deeds for you.” The man said: “Even my betrayals and my sins?” He said: “Yes.” And the man kept proclaiming “Allah is greatest” until he disappeared from sight. (Musnad Aḥmad; and Minhāj al-Qāṣidīn by Ibn Qudāma al-Maqdisī, Book of Repentance)

secs.t: “I have been forgiven”: another whisper
secs.h:
A person should not believe or assume that he has been forgiven; rather, he should fear Allah’s anger and hope for His mercy. This is what gives him the balance to keep going on his journey to Allah.

Satan may whisper to make you believe you have been forgiven, or that you have become righteous. When that happens, take refuge in Allah, never abandon the door of repentance, and strengthen your intention and resolve to stay away from the door of sin and to open the door of obedience.

Keep a sincere intention and a strong resolve to abandon sins and seek forgiveness, so that the door of repentance stays open — for that door closes whenever a person abandons it. Death may take him by surprise with his heart already sealed, if he misunderstood what it means to rely on Allah; he becomes blind to the path of righteousness and sees nothing but darkness.

Repentance is the key to many doors, and the open door to Allah’s mercy. So go through it and do not look back towards sin, or you will find yourself in Satan’s hands again. Allah gives us respite only out of His mercy — so let us weigh every one of our deeds.

aql.lead: A person does not sin with his seven members until a wrong thought enters his mind and he then intends, in his heart, to act on it. Sin begins as a spark, a small thought — and at that point it is easy to protect yourself. But if the thought turns into a flame, it takes hold of the heart and the mind, and the mind in turn drives the other members to commit the sin. This stage has ten levels, and the seeker trains for thirty days in each.

secs.t: Introduction: the mind is the key to protection
secs.h:
In this stage the seeker trains, in practice, to cleanse the mind of evil and satanic thoughts and to extinguish them when they come. In the later levels he trains to keep himself constantly occupied with the remembrance of Allah.

The mind is what the body of the aeroplane represents in the picture explained earlier, and it is the key to protection from Satan’s whispers:

  • Satan’s whispers are like storms, thunder and fiery winds that lead you astray, away from Allah’s path.
  • Every act of remembrance is a layer of protection — a layer of light that turns the lava and Satan’s whispers away from you.

In the end, whoever completes these ten levels will have purified his thoughts, and the remembrance of Allah and love of His Messenger ﷺ will be firmly rooted in his mind. When a person no longer takes pleasure in any wrong thought, it becomes easy for him to protect himself from sins.

secs.t: The two paths before the mind
secs.h:
Before the mind there are always two paths: one that leads to sin, and one that leads to safety from wrongdoing.

The path to sinHe lets the whisper slip quietly into his mind, unconcerned by the attack and taking no action against it.When evil is allowed to run on, it multiplies, grows and settles in the mind, until the mind leans towards the whisper and towards evil.The mind becomes absorbed in desires, then in sins, until they overpower it and it is hard to control — unless the person has a strong will and Allah’s care comes to his rescue.The whispers take over the mind until they overwhelm it; it gives in to evil and orders the members to commit it.Result: a mind darkened by indulging in sins, and a heart and spirit darkened by doing evil.
The path to safetyTwo weapons repel the attack of the whispers: seeking refuge in Allah from them, and resolve and will. With these, the burning of evil is easily put out.If the whisper comes back, he uses the same method again.Prevention: always guarding the mind against whispers by training himself in this method. Prevention grows slowly and keeps the mind safe from their corruption.Strengthening and increasing prevention: training the mind to reflect on Allah’s greatness and His mercy towards His creation, and to reflect on His Messenger ﷺ.Result: a mind constantly remembering Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, in which good thoughts flourish.

secs.t: Level one: rejecting the whispers
secs.h:
Never deliberately call up a wrong thought. If one comes to you from Satan or from the ego, do not knowingly dwell on it; instead seek refuge in Allah and turn your thoughts to Allah Most High, to the Messenger ﷺ, to the Hereafter, or to any permissible worldly task.

Do not attach yourself to the thought, and do not fight it either, so as not to make it bigger.

Example: if the idea of doing something bad occurs to you, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, then remember that this thought came to you only by Allah’s will, that He knows everything you think, and that He is able to punish you. You can also move your mind to a permissible worldly task, and say: “I believe in Allah and His Messenger.”

How does the aeroplane catch fire?

There are always two paths: one leads to disobedience and sin, the other to effort and nearness to Allah. When Satan’s whispers enter the mind, they are like a shower of lava sticking to the aeroplane. If the thought pleases you, the whispers sink in deeper and the lava begins to burn; if you leave it, it will burn the whole mind — the aeroplane — and you will commit the sin.

Every second counts, because every second puts the body of the aeroplane at risk until the mind is completely consumed.

Your two weapons on the path of good

  1. The shield of seeking refuge in Allah Almighty.
  2. The sword of willpower (or its water).

When the whispers — the lava — stick to the body of the aeroplane, use the weapon of seeking refuge and the water of willpower to defeat Satan and the fire of the whispers. The water of will stops the lava from sticking to the mind, and the mind builds a layer that resists the flames of evil and Satan’s whispers.

At this level: reject Satan’s whispers; do not think about anything ugly, do not enjoy it, and do not think about anything against the Sharia. Whenever the whispers try to enter your mind, put them out with the weapon of rejection.

secs.t: Level two: a supplication before every worldly task
secs.h:
Prayer, reciting the Quran and remembrance help a person remember Allah, whereas worldly tasks usually make him heedless of Him. Every worldly task carries the possibility of gain or loss, and gain and loss are in Allah’s hands and under His decree.

So at this level, before you begin any worldly task, first pray from your heart: “O Allah, protect me from its harm and let me benefit from it.” In this way every worldly task that makes a person forget Allah becomes a means of connecting him to Allah.

Examples:

  1. When you leave your house for any task, say: “O Allah, protect others from the harm of my self, bless me in my work, and protect me from the harm of others.”
  2. When a hardship befalls you, say: “O Allah, grant me patience with it, turn it away from me, and make it an expiation for my sins.”

secs.t: Level three: asking Allah’s permission
secs.h:
Picture Allah Most High as always with you, in your heart and mind, and ask His permission whenever you set out to do anything, religious or worldly. Then keep Allah’s name before your eyes and rely on Him. If you forget, remember and bring this conviction back to mind.

Begin by applying this level to your main activities, then gradually add smaller ones.

When a person believes that someone of high rank is with him, he naturally asks that person’s permission for matters that need it. The same applies to prayer, supplication, reciting the Quran, eating and sleeping: before you begin any act, bring Allah’s greatness to mind in your heart and say: “O Allah, I ask Your permission to do this, and I ask You to bless it.”

secs.t: Level four: the Prophetic supplications
secs.h:
At this level, once Allah is strongly present in your mind, you say the forty Prophetic supplications that the Messenger ﷺ used to repeat at various times — when eating, drinking, sleeping and dressing.

Example: for the situations that recur in your day, learn the Prophetic supplications that belong to them and say them at their proper times — the supplications for food, for drink, for leaving the house, for entering the market, for putting on clothes and for beginning work.

You will find them in “The Sunnahs of the Messenger ﷺ” among the app’s tools.

secs.t: Level five: from talking to yourself to talking with Allah
secs.h:
Keep up your awareness of Allah’s presence at all times: Allah sees me at every moment and in every place, and hears me at every moment and in every place.

Note down on paper the time you spend away from Allah’s company, so that you know how much of the twenty-four hours you spent with Allah and how much in heedlessness.

Most people, when awake, talk to themselves — some in words, most in thoughts: “Today I need to do this”, “I have to sort out my finances”, “My husband (or wife) is not happy”, “What will happen in the future? I will die anyway — will I go to Paradise or to Hell?” A person thinks all the time about his desires, worries and concerns for today, tomorrow, the future or the Hereafter, and in every case he is talking to himself.

At this level, instead of talking to yourself, talk to Allah about all your concerns, fears and wishes — past, present and future.

This practice and reflection bring great benefits:

  1. When a person talks to himself, his mind comes under pressure that pushes him towards depression, tension and nervous behaviour. But when he talks to Allah and calls upon Him, his mind is set free and less weighed down, because it lets go of its burdens.
  2. If a person keeps his thoughts to himself and talks only to himself, little changes, because a human being is limited. But if he voices them and lays them before Allah, the Mighty, whose power and knowledge have no limits, he begins to receive help and blessing in his life, moment by moment and day by day.
  3. Thinking only with oneself makes a person forget the remembrance of Allah and His presence, and then he is carried away by his concerns and fears. But by staying in contact and conversation with Allah, the All-Knowing, he gains the greatest benefit of all: his connection and relationship with Allah grow stronger, because he is in touch with his Lord all the time.

secs.t: Level six: reflecting on Allah’s signs
secs.h:
Allah Most High tells us in the Holy Quran that in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the existence of all creatures, there are signs that point to the Creator. So at this level the seeker trains to reflect deeply on creation and on the events connected to it, which helps him to remember Allah.

How to practise: reflect and ponder on seven different events you encounter each day, and write them down daily.

Example: if a person falls ill, that is a sign that life is temporary and that health and sickness are both in Allah’s hands. A person may neglect prayer or other religious matters because of worldly busyness, yet when he falls ill that busyness stops completely. Just as illness strikes suddenly, death too comes suddenly, unexpected and without warning. All matters are in Allah’s hands and under His decree, so a person should turn his focus and gaze towards Allah, trying to live his life by His commands alone.

secs.t: Level seven: positive thinking and good opinion
secs.h:
At this level the seekers’ minds are trained to become good and positive. A person benefits greatly from positive thinking, and through it reaches a high degree of nearness to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. This is also called “good opinion” (ḥusn al-ẓann), and it has three parts:

  1. Good opinion of Allah Most High.
  2. Good opinion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Sunnah.
  3. Good opinion of the believers.

The seeker begins by recognising that life is full of different events and that he must mix and deal with many people. On some unfortunate occasions things happen to him or to those around him that cause obstruction, annoyance or loss. Despite these negative experiences, he learns to look at them positively — provided that the negative act done to him is not itself a sin.

Example 1: you asked for help in a difficulty and were refused

Do not bear a grudge or hatred towards that person; look at it from another angle: had he helped you, you would have been under his favour and kindness, and Allah has freed you from that indebtedness. Remember too that helping you was not his duty — perhaps he had problems of his own, or lacked the means to help. In this way you learn not to let hatred and enmity enter your heart, and to pray for him instead.

Example 2: your car broke down on a journey

Instead of thinking “Why did this happen? What sin did I commit to deserve this?” and becoming aggressive with your passengers, believe that it is a blessing from Allah that your car did not break down on thousands of other journeys, that this is part of knowing Allah Most High, that this is far better for you, and that Allah has saved you from a greater problem. Anger and frustration do not solve the problem — they only make things worse.

secs.t: Level eight: avoiding negative thinking
secs.h:
At this level the seeker trains to avoid hypocritical, negative thinking about any event, incident or person.

If he thinks negatively without meaning to, he does not let the thought settle in his heart, but wipes it out with positive thinking.

Example: regarding worldly blessings, the seeker should not focus on those who have more wealth and possessions than he does, but look at those who have less wealth and fortune.

secs.t: Level nine: loving and obeying the Prophet ﷺ
secs.h:
At this level the seeker learns the Prophetic biography and thinks constantly of the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, for nearness to Allah Most High cannot be reached except through love of the Prophet ﷺ and obedience to him.

In addition, he follows outwardly the character of the Prophet ﷺ and his pure way of life, exactly as if you were living night and day in his company. He follows his way ﷺ in sleeping, waking, undressing and conducting business, and reflects on and imagines how the Prophet ﷺ did these things in his daily life.

secs.t: Level ten: as if you see Allah
secs.h:
At this level the seeker focuses his attention entirely on Allah and spends his whole life, night and day, as if Allah Most High were watching him, acting in reality as though Allah Most High were with him.

Two qualities must be reached at this level:

  1. Mental and spiritual awareness of, and focus on, Allah.
  2. Fitting actions that accompany this inner awareness of Him.

qalbIntro.lead: Besides purifying the body, its members and the mind, there are sins that cannot be seen with the eye, yet they are extremely dangerous and can lead a person to the Fire. Among them: rancour, hatred, arrogance, showing off and love of this world. In this stage we rid ourselves of these traits and replace them with praiseworthy ones, such as gratitude, humility, love of Allah and detachment (removing the craving for this world from the heart).

secs.t: The four states and the right response to each
secs.h:
A person spends his whole life in one or more of these four states:

  1. Obedience.
  2. Disobedience.
  3. Blessing.
  4. Hardship.

In this stage he learns how to deal rightly with each of these four states, and how to turn his state into mercy, so that he lives a good life:

  1. In obedience: humility, lowliness before Allah, servanthood and sincerity.
  2. In disobedience: remorse, shame, forgiving others, and repentance.
  3. In blessing: attributing the favour to Allah and thanking Him from the heart, using the blessing in line with Allah’s commands, and never using it to disobey Him.
  4. In hardship: patience, keeping away from sins, and returning to Allah.

The seeker trains in particular qualities to use in each state, which help him turn his state into a blessing from Allah, Glorified and Exalted:

Obedience→Servanthood→BlessingDisobedience→Repentance→BlessingBlessing→Gratitude→BlessingHardship→Patience→Blessing

Each of these has levels in which the seeker trains practically, mentally and spiritually.

secs.t: The seats: purifying the spirit
secs.h:
In the picture of the aeroplane, the seats stand for the third stage of purification: the praiseworthy qualities a person can acquire, all of them inner qualities of the servant. Each seat symbolises a good quality in a person. But some seats are torn and stained with filth, and those seats represent the qualities of Satan.

Clean seats: good qualitiesSincerityHumilityServanthoodGratitudePatience
Torn seats: Satan’s qualitiesConceitEnvyLove of this worldSelf-loveVanity

secs.t: The heavenly covenants: how to train
secs.h:
In this stage the seeker trains in the heavenly covenants, each of which has degrees:

  • The covenant of sincerity: seven degrees.
  • The covenant of humility: ten degrees.
  • The covenant of gratitude: seven degrees.
  • The covenant of repentance: five degrees.

Mark every day on which you fulfil the condition of the degree you are in, for thirty days. If you break one of the conditions, stop and start again, and write the number of your degree in the “mistakes column”.

qalbIntro.rules: Rules for keeping the covenant of

lv: All deeds, such as prayer and reciting the Quran, are performed by the seeker to gain Allah’s pleasure, salvation and reward in the Hereafter. He must make his intention sincere at the beginning, in the middle and at the end.

To do good deeds purely for the sake of Allah Most High — not merely out of desire, or because he feels he needs to do them. Some people perform acts that look like worship, but do them only out of desire and for the comfort they bring. Whoever does this should know and understand: we are not servants of our desires or our feelings — we are servants of Allah.
To do good deeds solely to gain Allah’s pleasure, not to gain Paradise.

To do good deeds for Allah alone, because Allah is the Lord of the worlds — not even for the sake of Allah’s pleasure itself, for that would still leave a need in his intention. In this way his deed becomes purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
That your worship be purely for Allah’s own sake, for the final destination — Paradise or the Fire — already lies in Allah’s prior knowledge.
That you worship Allah with no aim or motive.
To consider that you are striving to rise through the degrees of sincerity and trying to keep to this conduct all your life, and never to count yourself as sincere — for sincerity is a lofty station.
To think and believe that the least of the Muslims is better than you, and never to regard them as base or beneath you.
To purify and cleanse the heart of the rancour and hatred that come from worldly disputes, especially with your family and close friends.

To attribute every good deed you do to Allah Most High — that is, you are able to do it only by Allah’s grace and mercy — and in this way you become more humble. All knowledge of good and bad deeds was made clear by Allah through our master Muhammad ﷺ, and it is Allah who gave you the place, the time, the mind and the body that enable you to do good deeds. So the right response to doing good is not arrogance or self-admiration; rather, you should become more humble towards people.

That the seeker does good deeds for Allah alone, because Allah is the Lord of the worlds — not even for the sake of Allah’s pleasure itself, for that would still leave a need in his intention. In this way his deed becomes purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
That your worship be purely for Allah’s own sake, for the final destination — Paradise or the Fire — already lies in Allah’s prior knowledge.

When you see people — elderly, young or middle-aged — pray inwardly that Allah makes easy for them what is good for them at their age; for a young man, for example, that marriage be made easy for him. Or when you see a woman who is not Muslim, pray that she be guided to Islam.

To count and believe that every good and blessing that distinguishes you is not yours but a gift from Allah Most High — like a television screen, which displays images that come from outside and are not its own.
To consider that you are striving to rise through the degrees of humility and trying to keep to this conduct all your life, and never to count yourself as humble — for humility is a lofty station.
To believe that you fall short in worshipping Allah, that you cannot worship Him as He deserves, and that you are unable to fulfil Allah’s rights as they are due to Him.
To believe that we do not use the talents and abilities Allah gave us in serving Allah and His religion as fully as we should.

Whenever you are granted any blessing, physical or spiritual, attribute it to Allah Most High with your mind and your tongue, and acknowledge that Allah is the Giver of these blessings and good things. Never attribute them to yourself, thinking that what you have comes from your own ability and skill, and so forget Allah, the Merciful, the Giver.

When any misfortune, problem or disaster befalls you, try to see the hidden blessings within it and focus on its aspects of faith — for misfortunes carry hidden blessings from Allah. Do not be shaken and forget Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

When you see international disasters around you, in your region or in other countries, you will find blessings in them; look at them from a positive angle, for these calamities contain various blessings, lessons and admonitions from Allah Most High.
To thank Allah for the blessings He has given us in our social, environmental and financial life, from a worldly point of view.
To reflect on how a person can share his blessings with others, and to start doing so in practice — and to do it for Allah’s pleasure.

To consider that you are striving to rise through the degrees of gratitude and trying to keep to this conduct all your life, and never to count yourself as grateful — for gratitude is a lofty station.
To reflect and ponder: “Am I using any of Allah’s blessings to disobey Him?” — especially regarding the three levels.
To make amends to those whose rights you violated in the past, by restoring their rights and asking them to pardon and forgive you.
To leave bad company and wicked people.
To cut off every road that leads a person to sin.
To move away from a sinful way of life in dress, food and social relations, and replace it with a way of life that follows the Prophetic way.

The penitent must leave the sin outwardly and inwardly: outwardly by abandoning it, and inwardly by no longer thinking about it — not reliving any pleasure or thrill of past sins, and not wishing to commit them in the future; otherwise he will surely return to the road of sin.

ikhlas.lead: The aim of this journey is to please Allah and to succeed in the Hereafter. Whoever has other aims for the journey — winning people’s respect, making money or becoming famous — has made his journey worthless, and on the Day of Reckoning he will be held to strict account instead of being rewarded for his deeds.

secs.t: The aim of the journey
secs.h:
Whoever works for other than Allah will not see his effort and good deeds bear the hoped-for fruit; rather, he will be held to account, because his worship was for other than Allah — and this is a form of minor shirk.

So it is important to hold a good and sound intention in every deed, such as remembrance and worship, and to keep away from sins in order to please Allah alone, and to protect oneself from Hell to gain Paradise — whether or not people are pleased with you, whether or not they respect you, and whether or not you gain money or any other benefit, for worship of Allah is not harmed by such things.

On the other hand, if a person spends a little time doing small good deeds, or a few moments with a good intention to please Allah Almighty, he will be rewarded many times over, and that deed may be enough for his salvation.

As a ḥadīth relates, a sinful woman from an earlier nation gave water to a thirsty dog and was saved from the Fire by that deed. And it is reported that a man fought with his life in battle, yet on the Day of Resurrection he is dragged and thrown into Hell, and Allah Most High says to him: “You fought so that it would be said you were brave, and it has been said. You have no reward from Me today, for you did not sacrifice your life for My sake.”

That is why one should be among those who seek to please Allah Most High, not to please people.

secs.t: A great misunderstanding of sincerity and spiritual states
secs.h:
Many people do good deeds and strive when they set out on the journey of drawing near to Allah and seeking His pleasure, but through lack of knowledge Satan and the ego deceive them with a false idea, and they say to themselves:

“Why don’t we experience miracles and wonders as Allah’s close friends did, even though we have begun the spiritual journey, perform our remembrances and litanies, reflect on Allah’s dominion and follow the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ?”

They also believe they ought to see good dreams, or certain colours or lights during worship and meditation. When these things do not happen, they despair and think they have not been accepted. Sometimes they end up abandoning the path of obedience, worship and the Sunnah, and return to Satan’s way of life — if they have not consulted a competent teacher.

These people did not have a pure intention from the start, and they confused what is the goal with what is not. Their worship is not for Allah alone; they are seeking unveilings and wonders. Instead of being servants of Allah alone, they have become servants of wonders, servants of unveiling, servants of visions, servants of pleasure… and so on.

“And they were commanded only to worship Allah, devoting their religion purely to Him, as people of pure faith.” (al-Bayyina 98:5)

In this sense, the true servant’s task in this life is to worship his Lord without any conditions or incentives.

secs.t: An eye-opening event: Imam al-Shaʿrānī’s experience
secs.h:
Among the experiences of Imam ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Shaʿrānī (may Allah have mercy on him) — a very famous scholar, a friend of Allah and an imam in the science of purifying the soul — he relates:

“On the blessed Monday, the seventeenth of Rajab in the year nine hundred and thirty-one, a strong urge stirred in me to seek the stations of the friends of Allah (may Allah be pleased with them), and I came to despise everything I was in, and my life was troubled by it — for in that lay discontent with what Allah Most High had apportioned, so that I feared a bad ending, His displeasure and His anger. I went out aimlessly, and while I was in Fustat, opposite Rawda in Egypt, a state between sleep and waking took hold of me, and I heard a voice whose sound I could hear but whose owner I could not see, saying to me on behalf of the Truth, Glorified and Exalted: ‘My servant, if I showed you all of creation and the number of grains of sand, the name of every atom of it, the plants with their names and lifespans, the animals with their lifespans and their lineage back to their origins — beasts, birds, insects and all creatures — and unveiled for you the dominion of the heavens and the earth, Paradise and the Fire and all they contain, outwardly and inwardly; and if I sent down rain at your hand, and brought the dead to life at your hand, and caused to flow at your hand everything with which I have honoured My believing servants — you would have nothing of My servanthood.’”

Explanation: all these gifts and favours are among the blessings Allah Most High grants His servant, and the servant has no part or role in them at all. A person finds nearness to Allah when he does something that pleases Allah Most High in accordance with the Prophetic way (the Sunnah).

For example, if a person enters the bathroom in the way the Sunnah teaches, he wins a degree of nearness to Allah. Conversely, if he had all that was mentioned above but without obedience, he would find no nearness to Allah at all. Iblīs had — and still has — many supernatural powers, and the Antichrist too will have certain supernatural powers through sorcery and tricks, yet both are accursed.

Imam ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Shaʿrānī says: “When these words were complete, what the voice had cast upon me came to an end, and I was left with no craving for any station of the friends of Allah, in this world or the next — and I praised Allah Most High in gratitude for what He had bestowed.” (from the book: al-Anwār al-Qudsiyya fī Bayān Ādāb al-ʿUbūdiyya)

secs.t: The desire to be known for one’s deeds
secs.h:
It is true that people want others to know of their good deeds and merits. Just as there is an appetite for food, there is also an appetite for fame, appreciation and respect.

If you satisfy an appetite in a wrong, unlawful way — with forbidden food or with drugs — it is forbidden and sinful. But if you satisfy the same need in a lawful, permissible way, you will be rewarded for it. In the same way, there is no sin in the essence of fame or appreciation; what makes it good or bad, sin or virtue, is how this desire is satisfied.

The lawful way: satisfy your need to be seen, known, heard of and appreciated by thinking that:

  • Allah, the All-Seeing, sees you.
  • Allah, the All-Hearing, hears your every word and whisper.
  • Allah, the All-Knowing, knows your thoughts, your circumstances and your deeds.
  • Allah, the Appreciative (who thanks His servant), will value you and reward your deed as no one else can.

Then you will be rewarded for satisfying your desire for recognition in a lawful way known as sincerity.

Conversely: if you satisfy your desire to be known, seen, praised and talked about by people, this is a sin and minor shirk — it means you sought people’s praise through worship. Outwardly you worship Allah, but inwardly you worship people; this is sincerity neither to Allah nor to people.

If you have found a lawful, good way to satisfy this desire, why satisfy it in an unlawful, harmful way? People have no power to benefit you, and Allah Most High will not reward you, because it was not purely for His sake. That way you lose in this world and the next; whereas if you do your deeds with a sincere intention, you will be rewarded in this world and the next. Think deeply and reflect on this.

secs.t: How do we achieve sincerity?
secs.h:
Sincerity will not come to you by reading about it in books or lessons; you will gain knowledge about sincerity, but not sincerity itself. You must take one more step forward: putting sincerity into practice through vigilance (murāqaba).

In every good deed you do, think from the depth of your heart that Allah’s creatures cannot benefit you or harm you in anything Allah has not written for you, and that you are doing this for Allah’s sake alone and to gain His pleasure — for in His hand are honour and disgrace, gain and loss, death and life… and so on.

secs.t: The first stage of sincerity
secs.h:
Check your intention at the beginning, in the middle and at the end of all your acts of worship; if you do not, there is no guarantee or certainty that your deed will be sincere or accepted.

Imagine your deeds as a cake you have to bake: if the dough is not good at the start, the result will be bad; if it burns or overcooks in the middle, the result will be bad too; and if all goes well at the start and in the middle but it is exposed to too much heat at the end, the result will still be bad and unusable.

To train yourself in patience and keep up your self-review, use the ikhlas sheet for ninety days in a row; after that you can continue to the second stage of sincerity, then the third, up to the seventh.

g1.h: Giving priority to Allah and His obedience
g1.def: To be in complete obedience to Allah’s commands: worshipping Him alone, taking no other gods beside Him, and giving all His commands priority over any other command — so that Allah and His commands come first in your life.
g1.ev: “Say: indeed my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner; this I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit.” <small>(al-Anʿām 6:162–163)</small>
g1.sign: Hastening to the obligatory acts at their times, and stopping at the limits Allah has set.

g2.t: Revering the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
g2.h: Giving priority to love of the Prophet ﷺ and following his Sunnah
g2.def: To give priority to following the life of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over every other way of life, and to love the Messenger ﷺ more than you love all of creation — yourself included.
g2.ev: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you truly believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child and all people.” <small>(al-Bukhārī and Muslim)</small> And when ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) told him, “You are dearer to me than everything except myself,” he said: “No — by Him in whose hand is my soul — not until I am dearer to you than yourself.” <small>(al-Bukhārī)</small>
g2.sign: Caring for the Sunnahs and voluntary acts, and sending abundant blessings upon him ﷺ.

g3.def: To show mercy and kindness to all creatures: helping people and serving the environment with your wealth, your possessions and your loyalty, and protecting humans and jinn from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection by reminding them of the ways to success in the light of the Quran and the Sunnah.
g3.ev: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in heaven will be merciful to you.” <small>(Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī)</small>
g3.sign: Charity, meeting people’s needs, a kind word, and inviting to good with wisdom.

g4.def: To keep in mind, remember, feel and believe that you are with the Creator: that Allah watches your every movement and knows what passes through your mind, and that He is with you wherever you are and in whatever situation.
g4.ev: “And He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees what you do.” <small>(al-Ḥadīd 57:4)</small> And in the ḥadīth of Gabriel (peace be upon him): “Excellence (iḥsān) is to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He surely sees you.” <small>(Muslim)</small>
g4.sign: Remembering Allah with the heart in every state, and being mindful of Him in private and in public.
